claim: DGAT1 and DGAT2 are TG synthesis enzymes
source: We generated mice lacking both known TG synthesis enzymes, DGAT1 and DGAT2 (Cases et al., 1998; Cases et al., 2001), in adipocytes.
evidence: Supported by citations to Cases et al., 1998 and Cases et al., 2001

claim: ADGAT DKO mice were generated by crossing adipose tissue-specific Dgat1 knockout mice with Dgat2 flox mice
source: To generate adipose tissue-specific Dgat1 and Dgat2 double-knockout (ADGAT DKO) mice, we crossed adipose tissue-specific Dgat1 knockout mice (Cre-transgene expressed under control of the mouse adiponectin promoter [Eguchi et al., 2011] with Dgat2 flox mice [Chitraju et al., 2019])
evidence: Supported by citations to Eguchi et al., 2011 and Chitraju et al., 2019, describing the generation method

claim: Dgat1 mRNA levels were decreased by ~95% in iWAT and BAT of ADGAT DKO mice
source: Validation of gene knockouts showed mRNA levels of Dgat1 were decreased by ~95% and Dgat2 by ~90% in both inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) and interscapular brown adipose tissue (BAT) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: Dgat2 mRNA levels were decreased by ~90% in iWAT and BAT of ADGAT DKO mice
source: Validation of gene knockouts showed mRNA levels of Dgat1 were decreased by ~95% and Dgat2 by ~90% in both inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) and interscapular brown adipose tissue (BAT) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: DGAT1 and DGAT2 proteins were absent in iWAT and BAT of ADGAT DKO mice
source: Western blot analysis showed that DGAT1 and DGAT2 proteins were absent in iWAT and BAT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: In vitro DGAT activity in lysates of adipose tissue of ADGAT DKO mice was decreased by ~80% in iWAT
source: In vitro DGAT activity in lysates of adipose tissue of ADGAT DKO mice was decreased by ~80% in iWAT and ~95% in BAT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by enzyme activity assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: In vitro DGAT activity in lysates of adipose tissue of ADGAT DKO mice was decreased by ~95% in BAT
source: In vitro DGAT activity in lysates of adipose tissue of ADGAT DKO mice was decreased by ~80% in iWAT and ~95% in BAT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by enzyme activity assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: In vitro DGAT activity in isolated adipocytes of iWAT was decreased by ~80% in ADGAT DKO mice
source: Similarly, in vitro DGAT activity in isolated adipocytes of iWAT was decreased by ~80% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by enzyme activity assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: ADGAT DKO mice appeared healthy
source: ADGAT DKO mice appeared healthy (Figure 1A)
evidence: Supported by visual observation shown in Figure 1A

claim: ADGAT DKO mice yielded offspring with the predicted Mendelian ratio of genotypes
source: ADGAT DKO mice appeared healthy (Figure 1A) and yielded offspring with the predicted Mendelian ratio of genotypes.
evidence: Supported by breeding data

claim: Fat depots were decreased in chow-fed ADGAT DKO mice
source: Nuclear magnetic resonance imaging showed that fat depots were decreased in chow-fed ADGAT DKO mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by NMR imaging data shown in Figure 1B

claim: Body weights of 12-week-old chow-fed control mice and ADGAT DKO mice were similar
source: Body weights of 12-week-old chow-fed control mice (Dgat1 and Dgat2 double-flexed mice, D1D2 flox) and ADGAT DKO mice were similar (Figure 1C)
evidence: Supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1C

claim: Fat mass was decreased by ~60% in 12-week-old ADGAT DKO mice
source: Body weights of 12-week-old chow-fed control mice (Dgat1 and Dgat2 double-flexed mice, D1D2 flox) and ADGAT DKO mice were similar (Figure 1C), but dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) analysis revealed that the fat mass was decreased by ~60% in ADGAT DKO mice.
evidence: Supported by DEXA analysis data shown in Figure 1C

claim: Fat mass was reduced by ~75% in 1-year-old ADGAT DKO mice
source: The reduction in fat mass was persistent: DEXA analysis of 1-year-old ADGAT DKO mice showed that the fat mass was reduced by ~75% and that lean mass was increased by ~15% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by DEXA analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E

claim: Lean mass was increased by ~15% in 1-year-old ADGAT DKO mice
source: The reduction in fat mass was persistent: DEXA analysis of 1-year-old ADGAT DKO mice showed that the fat mass was reduced by ~75% and that lean mass was increased by ~15% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by DEXA analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E

claim: Visceral white adipose tissue depots were markedly atrophied in ADGAT DKO mice
source: Visceral white adipose tissue (WAT) depots (gonadal, mesenteric, pericardial, and perirenal fat depots) were markedly atrophied in ADGAT DKO mice (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by visual observation shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F

claim: Gonadal WAT and subcutaneous iWAT in ADGAT DKO mice appeared distinctly 'beige' in color
source: Gonadal WAT (gWAT) and subcutaneous iWAT in ADGAT DKO mice appeared distinctly 'beige' in color (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by visual observation shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F

claim: iWAT and BAT of ADGAT DKO mice were denser and sank in a liquid fixative
source: In ADGAT DKO mice, iWAT and BAT were denser, as demonstrated by their sinking in a liquid fixative (Figure 1F).

claim: gWAT and iWAT of ADGAT DKO mice contain multi-locular lipid droplets in adipocytes

claim: Lipid droplets in iWAT of ADGAT DKO mice stain with BODIPY

evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1G

claim: WAT of ADGAT DKO mice contain triglycerides

claim: Phospholipid levels were increased in iWAT of ADGAT DKO mice
source: Increased phospholipid levels in iWAT of ADGAT DKO mice. Lipids in iWAT were extracted and quantified by mass spectrometry (n=8).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1I

claim: The interscapular BAT depot in ADGAT DKO mice appeared darker brown than that in control mice
source: The interscapular BAT depot in ADGAT DKO mice appeared darker brown than that in control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by visual observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A

claim: TGs and LDs were undetectable in BAT of ADGAT DKO mice

claim: BAT of chow-fed ADGAT DKO mice took up more glucose than BAT of control mice after injection of β-3-adrenoceptor agonist
source: Positron emission tomography-computed tomography scanning using 18-fluoro-deoxyglucose (18-FDG-PET/CT) showed that, after injection of β-3-adrenoceptor agonist (CL 316,243), BAT of chow-fed ADGAT DKO mice took up more glucose than BAT of control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D)

claim: Glycogen levels in BAT of ADGAT DKO mice were increased in all conditions except 4°C cold exposure
source: In agreement with increased glucose uptake, glycogen levels in BAT of ADGAT DKO mice were increased in all conditions except 4°C cold exposure (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).

claim: DGAT1 and DGAT2 appear to account for most of TG synthesis in mice
source: DGAT1 and DGAT2 appear to account for most of TG synthesis in mice.
evidence: Supported by inference from the literature and experimental observations

claim: Newborn mice lacking both DGAT enzymes have >95% reduction in whole body TGs
source: Newborn mice lacking both DGAT enzymes have >95% reduction in whole body TGs (Stone et al., 2004)

source: adipocytes derived from fibroblasts lacking both enzymes fail to accumulate TGs or LDs (Harris et al., 2011).

claim: WAT of 8-week-old ADGAT DKO mice showed fewer and much smaller LDs than control WAT

claim: ADGAT DKO mice activate alternate pathways to accumulate neutral lipids
source: However, by age 15 weeks, ADGAT DKO mice exhibited more LDs in iWAT than 8-week-old ADGAT DKO mice, suggesting that they activate alternate pathways to accumulate neutral lipids (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).

claim: The neutral lipid that accumulated in ADGAT DKO mice was BODIPY-positive

claim: The TG content of iWAT in HFD-fed ADGAT DKO mice remained ~70% less than control mice

claim: Several phospholipids were substantially increased in iWAT of ADGAT DKO mice
